chapter_title: Chương 236: 0238【Đào Tuyết Muốn Đến Kinh Thành Du Lịch Tốt Nghiệp】

segments.title: Chương 236: 0238【Đào Tuyết Muốn Đến Kinh Thành Du Lịch Tốt Nghiệp】
segments.content:
Noon, on the second day of the Gaokao.

Guo Feng had used a company car once, and no one knew where he had gone. When he returned in the afternoon, he burst into Chen Guiliang's office, beaming and carrying something.

"Guess what's in here," Guo Feng asked, lifting the bag.

Chen Guiliang glanced at the shopping bag. The words "Shuangshun Qipao Shop" were printed on it, and he was instantly astonished. "Don't tell me you have a penchant for wearing women's clothing? And qipaos, no less!"

"What women's clothing? This is my academic gown. I'm graduating from university next month." Guo Feng took out the garment as if presenting a treasure.

Chen Guiliang asked, "A custom-made Chinese-style academic gown?"

Guo Feng nodded and said, "That's right. I thought graduation should be a bit more unique, so I went online to search for all kinds of academic gowns. I ended up finding a lot of news about Chinese-style ones. quite a few media outlets were reporting on it back in April."

"You're not usually one to care about appearances," Chen Guiliang said.

Guo Feng argued, "This isn't about appearance; it holds special meaning. Not only did I have one made for myself, but I also dragged Dong Qianqiu along to get one. But all we could find online were design drawings, we couldn't find any factories or shops. In the end, we took the designs to a qipao shop. The tailor there didn't know how to make it either. We said we could pay extra, and only then was the qipao tailor willing to give it a try."

As he spoke, he had already taken out the Chinese-style academic gown and put it on directly over his T-shirt and jeans.

"Uh... It's a bit of a mishmash. To put it nicely, you could call it a fusion of Chinese and Western styles," Chen Guiliang commented.

This was the Chinese-style academic gown designed by Xishan Qinkuang, the first bar owner of the Hanfu Tieba. Besides being posted on the Hanfu Tieba, it was also published on Tianhan.net. Back in April, it had already caused a small-scale buzz, with more than twenty media outlets reporting on it.

But the cap wasn't much different from a Western-style mortarboard, especially with the tassel specifically designed for the tassel-turning ceremony. Next was the large school emblem on the chest, which was particularly jarring. And then there were the Western-style leather shoes.

This fusion of Chinese and Western design looked somewhat incongruous.

Xishan Qinkuang was already working on designing a second version. He decided to no longer cater to Western customs and to create a series of purely Chinese-style academic gowns.

Chen Guiliang thought it looked bad, but Guo Feng was extremely pleased with it.

This guy was often unkempt, yet at times he could be incredibly flamboyant.

It was during work hours, and Guo Feng strutted around the company wearing the Chinese-style academic gown.

"Mr. Guo," an employee greeted him.

Guo Feng said with a smile, "You think my academic gown looks good too, huh?"

The employee was stunned for a moment. "Ah? Oh, it looks good, very handsome."

Guo Feng elaborated, "I had it custom-made at a qipao shop. I paid a lot extra before the tailor was willing to make it. Dong Qianqiu from Youke downstairs has one too. I took him to get it made with me."

The employee looked it over carefully and did indeed find it quite eye-catching. It was a shame he had already graduated, otherwise he would have definitely gotten one to show off.

After chatting for a bit, Guo Feng moved on to other workstations.

"Hello, Mr. Guo."

"Don't you think my academic gown is really cool?"

"Extremely cool."

"Haha, I had an old master tailor at a qipao shop custom-make it for me."

It had been a long time since Guo Feng had acted crazy. An intermittent episode like this was understandable.

Finally, he ran over to Ao Yanchang.

Ao Yanchang was also graduating next month. He asked with an envious look, "Damn, where did you buy this outfit?"

Guo Feng tirelessly explained, "You can't buy it ready-made. I had someone custom-make it."

Ao Yanchang quickly asked, "How much? Is there a women's version? I want to get one made too."

Guo Feng shook his head. "It's not about the money. The old tailor spent a full two months making this gown. There are only about 40 days left until the graduation ceremony. It's too late for you to order one now."

"That's not necessarily true. If they work overtime, they can definitely finish it," Ao Yanchang said.

This was true. As long as you paid enough, it could be done.

Besides, the old tailor was inexperienced the first time. Now that he had experience, he could save a lot of time.

Ao Yanchang asked for the address and phone number of the qipao shop, deciding to charge over there after work today.

After chatting with Ao Yanchang for a while, Guo Feng continued to wander around the company.

Xie Yang watched with envy.

He was currently on a leave of absence from school; God only knew when he would graduate.

However, after the university learned that he had become a senior executive at Bytedance, they agreed to extend his leave of absence, allowing him to resume his studies at any time.

Chen Guiliang stood at the door of his office, watching Guo Feng wander around everywhere, not knowing whether to laugh or cry.

Damn it, I'm going to get a set too when I graduate!

And the style has to be purely Chinese.

For no other reason than to show off.

Chen Guiliang returned to his office and searched for Tianhan.net and Hanfu Tieba.

These two websites were also key promotional targets for "Legends of the Three Kingdoms." Last year, Youke would post there every now and then. Many users from Tianhan.net and Hanfu Tieba had been converted into "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" players.

Chen Guiliang registered an account on Tianhan.net with the ID "Dream of a Billion Girls Worldwide."

He was bored out of his mind and posted a thread: "Has anyone recreated the Ming Dynasty feiyufu? The kind of bestowed robe recorded in the 'History of Ming.' High-ranking Jinyiwei wore it too. It would look especially cool paired with a xiuchun dao."

Chen Guiliang couldn't wait until graduation. He wanted to get a feiyufu outfit, sling a xiuchun dao over his shoulder, and stroll around the Peking University campus.

Clearly, the Hanfu revival movement was still in its very early stages at this time.

The first netizen to reply actually asked, "Is the feiyufu also a type of Hanfu?"

Chen Guiliang occasionally wrote novels at the company, and he had an e-book of the "History of Ming" saved on his computer.

He directly opened the "History of Ming" and copy-pasted: "'History of Ming, Records of Chariots and Attire': In the thirteenth year of the Zhengde reign, the emperor returned to the capital... First-rank officials wore embroidered douniu, second-rank officials wore embroidered feiyu, third-rank officials wore embroidered mang, fourth and fifth-rank officials wore embroidered qilin, and sixth and seventh-rank officials wore embroidered hubiao..."

In this era, all kinds of information were not yet readily available everywhere.

Just by posting a segment of the original text, Chen Guiliang was regarded by netizens as being very impressive: "Welcome, welcome, our forum has another expert. But your username... isn't it a bit too narcissistic?"

Another netizen asked, "Isn't the mang pao second only to the dragon robe? Why are the douniu and feiyu ranked above the mang pao?"

Chen Guiliang explained, "The douniu is a type of dragon. The feiyu is a python-like creature with a dragon's head. Their rank is higher than the python."

"Thank you, expert, for clearing that up."

"Are all the newcomers this knowledgeable these days? Brother, are you a history major?"

Before long, the moderators of Tianhan.net also came to reply in the thread.

However, after discussing for a long time, they were still stuck at the "feiyu pattern" stage.

No one knew what the feiyufu looked like.

This was something that would have to wait until the archival materials of the former Kong Family Mansion collection were made public before Hanfu enthusiasts could truly recreate it. Otherwise, they could only rely on guesswork.

After chatting with the moderators for a bit, Chen Guiliang suggested, "On this Tianhan Forum, you guys shouldn't just focus on Hanfu. You can also branch out into other cultural aspects, like ancient Chinese games—shuanglu, touhu, and so on. Discuss and recreate them online, and then play them directly at offline events. Yue Fei was a touhu enthusiast. This kind of game is very easy to recreate."

The moderators thought it made sense and invited Chen Guiliang to join the admin team.

But Chen Guiliang replied with, "Anyone who hasn't played 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' can download it and give it a try."

Everyone was floored, assuming Chen Guiliang was a promoter for "Legends of the Three Kingdoms."

Chen Guiliang added another line: "The fourth and fifth volumes of my 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty' are scheduled for official publication in mid-August. If you have the time and money, please show your support."

As soon as this was written, a wave of replies instantly flooded in.

"Chen Guiliang?"

"Damn it, how long have you been overdue with 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty'?"

"No wonder you're so knowledgeable about Ming dynasty attire. Turns out you're a historical novelist."

"Mr. Chen, I'm a 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' player. I'm a loyal fan of yours!"

"Spotted Chen Shi Yi, I'm going to post about this on Hanfu Tieba!"

"Getting up close to pat Mr. Chen's doggy head."
